title: Custom widgets without custom code
content:
Not every new widget needs a plugin. Many useful blocks are just a heading, a list and a little conditional markup that already exists in your template.

Start from a built-in widget

Duplicate a nearby widget in the layout editor, give it a clear title and choose a type that matches the data you need. The preview renderer already knows how to handle the standard Blogger widget types.

Reuse defaults

Default includables are your friend. A small b:includable can format every item in a collection, while b:include keeps the calling markup short and readable.

Validate before styling

Run the build after each structural change. Widget markup that parses cleanly is much easier to style than markup that only looks correct in the editor.
excerpt: Use built-in widget types and default includables to extend a template safely.
